title: AI trading mentor that reviews your trades against your own rules — free beta, web + mobile, no signals
author: TheOneTrueSax

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Good instinct grading against adherence instead of P&L. Almost everyone building this scores the outcome and then wonders why their users learn nothing.

Rule drift will bite you though: someone rewrites a rule after a loss so the last trade comes out compliant, and four weeks in the score tracks a moving target. Version the rule set and stamp each review with the version it graded against. That also hands the user something worth seeing, the week they quietly loosened their own stop rule.

Are you versioning them already, or is the rule set just the latest state of the conversation?

replies.author: TheOneTrueSax
replies.body:
Thank you, yes everyone sees a good day as green but if you got there then wrong way it's not sustainable.

That is a great point on the rule drift and versioning them. Never something I thought of. Also works in the positive way, if the coaching helps to tighten a rule you can retrospectively see anything that may have impacted things. Really appreciate the input

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the retrospective read is harder than it looks though. you tighten a rule and the next forty trades happen in a different market, so the rule looks good or bad for reasons that have nothing to do with the rule. we date stamp changes and just accept the comparison is dirty.

replies.author: TheOneTrueSax
replies.body: Yes that is a very fair point. Just planning out the rule versioning now. 🙂

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: nice. the annoying part is deciding what counts as a new version versus an edit, and you want that settled before you have forty of them.

replies.author: TheOneTrueSax
replies.body: So I think that would have to be a classification call. Could probably do something like a jaccard check prior to routing to a classification call, wouldn't need a anything too heavy weight for that check.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: A cheap prefilter makes sense. Watch what it does to paraphrases though, two people writing the same rule in different words score low on jaccard and go down the expensive path anyway, which is the case you were trying to dodge. What threshold are you running it at?

replies.author: TheOneTrueSax
replies.body: Not running anything yet not at my PC to get it running yet. Will run some tests prior to implementation
